Peru Recovers After Massive Floods Disrupt Economy; All Operations Resume

LIMA, Peru, June 15 – Economic activities across Peru have fully resumed after severe flooding swept through multiple regions last week, government officials announced Saturday. The disaster, caused by torrential rains linked to a late-season coastal storm, inundated major transport corridors and disrupted mining, agriculture, and logistics operations nationwide.

According to the National Institute of Civil Defense (INDECI), floodwaters peaked on June 7, inundating highways, halting rail and truck freight, and temporarily closing ports at Callao and Paita. Inland, communities from Piura in the north to Arequipa in the south faced power outages and evacuations affecting more than 50,000 people.

"Thanks to coordinated emergency response and swift repairs, all major infrastructure is now operational," said Julio Ríos, Peru’s Minister of Transport and Communications. "Road and rail networks are fully restored, and freight is moving without restriction."

The mining sector, a key driver of Peru’s economy, reported no lasting impact. “Production at all affected sites has resumed, and export schedules are back on track,” said Luz Marín, spokesperson for the Peruvian Mining Council. Agriculture unions confirmed that logistics bottlenecks have cleared, and fruit and coffee shipments are again reaching ports.

The Lima Chamber of Commerce estimates the floods caused temporary economic losses of $72 million, mostly due to short-term transportation delays. Analysts say recovery was accelerated by emergency infrastructure funds released on June 9.

"There are no remaining delays, shortages, or closures in any sector," said Rafael Huamán, analyst at MacroAndes Research. "The rapid reopening of ports and roads was crucial for the national recovery."

Authorities report that power and water services are fully restored, and schools and businesses in all affected areas have reopened. The government has pledged additional support to reinforce infrastructure against future events.
